whatItFakes: Another state's budget year after the opening is a view of its ledger in the country tier: its income, profit and general sales tax lines and its spending are the state government's share of the tier's state-and-local figures, a share fixed from the published lines at the tier's first month; every other revenue line (selective sales taxes, property, fees, federal aid and the rest) is held at its published opening value as an estimate, and spending keeps the published mix of lines. No act of the legislature adds to a spending line, and no money is paid.
why: The tier models only the income, profit and sales taxes and keeps state and local governments together; only the town's chain has treasuries and a budget process, and the other states' legislatures pass acts as results (world-legislating) and no budget bill yet.
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: Each spending line moved by the state's enacted acts and formulas (aid rules, enrollment, caseload), reserves and debt service, and the legislature's budget act as a result; money paid when a state is opened.

whatItFakes: A disaster elsewhere in the country is one result row (state, kind, start day, number of counties) from FEMA's recorded history; its federal aid reaches the state's budget and its job losses reach the state's regional months, both sized from FEMA's record when it is opened, but it has no damage built from the state's housing stock, building codes or budgets, no declaration by a governor or the President, and no reaction in national press or approval.
why: Damage should come from the housing stock, building codes, levees and budgets in force, the declaration from the governor's and the President's decisions, and aid from real treasuries (CTO ruling, Nov 8, 12:21 on #7365); those engines exist only for the town.
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: Detail built on open from the housing, budget and executive engines (damage, aid, the governor's and President's declarations), severity from the state's recorded spread, and the national press and approval reading the result.

whatItFakes: Inside the record (to Oct 9, 2026) the country's and the town's disasters are FEMA's real ones on their real days. After it they come from the climate's hazard levels (flood, storm, wildfire only: heat and drought have no recorded history), but each takes the days and figures of a recorded disaster of its state, or of the town's county, and hazard in turn, so the counties, the aid and the damaged homes it shows are a past disaster's, not the new one's.
why: The zero-dice guard allows no new draw, and the hazard calendar after the record needs a GENERATION entry in the list-pick inventory and per-county monthly hazard rates, which are not built (owner, Oct 16: both FEMA's records and the world's own conditions; after the records end, the game keeps making its own weather).
replacement: Detail built on open from the causes: the counties the hazard's level struck, the housing stock, building codes and budgets in force (SG-NATION-disaster-damage-from-causes).

whatItFakes: Another state's ballot measure result is kept as a result and enacts its law, but the press does not print the result itself: the measure-result bank has no place slot, so it would read as local news.
why: The English engine's measure-result pieces say "Voters approved {purpose}" with no place; the law the measure enacts reaches the national press through the law-took-effect story.
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: Measure-result bank pieces with a place (Words and Story), then this early return is deleted.

whatItFakes: The warming-to-hazard links use one size for every county: drought from the Southwest's vapor-pressure rise, wildfire from western forest studies, heat from a doubling over half a degree (no range); storm and flood from global and national figures converted to a per-degree size.
why: The National Climate Assessment and IPCC pages could not be fetched, and no source found gives a United States per-degree figure for heat, wildfire or drought by region or season.
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: Sizes by region and season from the National Climate Assessment (2023) chapters and the Littell et al. (2009) ecoprovince figure.

whatItFakes: A county's recorded hazard history is its FEMA declarations (flood, storm, wildfire); heat and drought have none (FEMA declared one drought), so their recorded rate is none and the climate's heat and drought levels move nothing until a history is read.
why: The NOAA Storm Events episodes (excessive heat, drought) by county were not fetched; FEMA's record is what the disasters module holds.
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: Counts of NOAA storm episodes (excessive heat, extreme heat, drought) by county, hazard and season in hazard-history.json, built by the same script.

whatItFakes: The rest of the world's fossil CO2 follows a straight line between three published points (38.1 Gt in 2025, 35 in 2035, 30 in 2050, held flat after) and does not respond to any other country's law, price or event; its spread (flat near 38 Gt under current policies) is not run.
why: No year-by-year published scenario path was reachable; the IEA pages returned 403 and the points come from a search summary.
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: The IEA or IPCC scenario table by year, with other countries' own laws moving their share.

whatItFakes: FEMA records how many homes a disaster damaged in a town but not whose; the homes marked damaged are the owners' homes of the weakest kinds (mobile home, farmhouse, house, rowhouse, apartment) and then the lowest valued, and each damaged household takes an equal part of the town's FEMA aid and repair bill.
why: The records carry a count and a town total, not a home-by-home list; no construction-age, flood-zone or insurance record is kept for a household's home yet.
replacement: Damage by each home's build year, kind, flood zone and insurance from the housing record, aid by each household's own FEMA award, and repairs by the household's own bill.

whatItFakes: The President's view of a federal order is their view of the nearest question the stance data records (for the power-plant carbon rule, state carbon pricing), because the stance axes are measured from the states' laws and a federal question has no state answers to correlate; the federal series list holds one order, and the played President has no screen to issue it yet.
why: issue-axes-2026.json is measured across the states' recorded answers; no poll-based axis for federal questions is kept, and only the power-plant series is both set by a President in practice and read by an engine.
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: A measured or polled left-right axis for each federal question (Pew and Gallup by party), more orders and rules in federal-orders.json (the refugee admissions determination), and the played President's screen over federalOrderable.

whatItFakes: Every number in the country tier's rules (how much of income each fifth spends, each sector's pay share, how fast firms adjust staff and prices, how strongly movers answer pay and work) is a value set by hand near a figure the builder knew, not one fitted to a published series.
why: The tier was built on Nov 10, 2026 to replace the national formula; the values were chosen so a 40-year run with the central bank's own view stays calm and the tax, disaster and rate twins answer. BLS and Census hosts were blocked from the building session.
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: A research pass (pool item core-country-tier-numbers-sourced) that fetches each figure's table, sets the value with its citation and spread, and re-runs the model's own test.

whatItFakes: A metro area or the rest of a state has no households, employers or ledger of its own: it keeps the difference from its state that it opened with, and its jobs, pay, people and prices move exactly as its state's do.
why: The country tier's first slice holds 56 states. Splitting each into its regions multiplies the cells by about 2.4 and needs each region's own sector mix and budget lines read in.
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: Cells and a ledger for each region inside its state (the regional data already holds each region's people and sector mix), stepped by the same month, with the state as their sum.

whatItFakes: The nation's spending beyond the benefits the cells receive (its own purchases, aid to the states, interest) is one figure fitted so the federal books balance on day one, which then follows prices and sales. No budget is adopted and no deficit is run at the opening.
why: The federal budget engine in the played world is the town's own chain's; the tier has no federal budget lines by state yet (data/research/federal/federal-spending-by-state-fy2024.json is not read).
replacement: Resolved (pool item core-country-tier-federal-budget-reaches-the-states, Nov 11, 2026): the fitted figure is deleted. The tier's federal ledger reads the federal budget in force line by line (federalSpendingReader in src/core2/country-law.ts), each line shared among the states by population times the world's stake in it (data/research/federal/federal-spending-by-state-fy2024.json) and sent where it pays (src/core2/data/country/federal-lines.json): household lines scale the cells' benefits, purchase lines are bought from the state's sectors, interest and aid abroad leave the cells. The nation now runs the deficit its budget gives. Shown in tests/golden-path/federal-dollar.node-test.ts.

whatItFakes: Each state adopts next year's budget equal to the revenue it took in over the last twelve months, every twelfth month of the run. No legislature decides it, no reserve is drawn or built, and its unmodeled lines only keep up with prices.
why: Other states' legislatures keep one tally a session and no budget process (pool items nation-other-states-change-laws-in-year-one-then-almost-never and nation-other-states-never-change-an-amount).
replacement: Each state's budget from its own legislature's act on its fiscal calendar, reading its balanced-budget law and its reserve, written to this ledger.

whatItFakes: The world outside the country buys a little more each year at prices that rise a little each year, both at fixed rates. Nothing abroad ever changes.
why: No engine keeps the rest of the world. The national events engine records disasters, not price shocks from abroad.
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: Recorded events abroad (a price shock, a slump, a tariff) from the national events engine, read by the tier's outside demand and prices.

whatItFakes: People moving between states are kept twice: the country tier moves its cells by pay after tax, prices and work, and the counted-moves engine still keeps its own count of each state's people beside it. Its arrivals are fitted to the survey once, at the opening, and then follow taxes, prices and work; the monthly re-fit is gone.
why: Replacing the counted-moves engine's state counts with the tier's cells touches 1,800 lines that also move the town's own households; it ships as the next pull request so this one stays reviewable.
replacement: Pool item core-country-tier-moves-one-holder: the counted-moves engine reads each state's people and place constants from the tier, and its pinned departures are deleted.

whatItFakes: A town or county worker the records place at no employer (the opening's workers outside a recorded firm, commuters among them), or at an employer whose classification and kind have no sector in the tables, is counted in the state's sectors in the shares the state's jobs are in, not in the industry they work in.
why: The opening records those workers only as a count per household and pays them from the place's outside account; no record says which industry they work in.
replacement: Each such worker's industry drawn at the opening from the county's recorded employment by sector (the survey the county sample already reads) and kept on the household, with every employer classification given a row in business-books.json or src/core2/data/country/employer-sectors.json.

whatItFakes: When the played town and its county are taken out of their state, the state's government books and what its owners are paid leave in proportion to the people taken out, and each sector's cash, sales and buyers in proportion to the jobs taken out; they are not read from the town's own treasuries, firms' books and sales.
why: The country tier's cells hold a state's governments and firms as one ledger and one cell per sector; the town's treasuries and firms keep their own books in other units and no reader yet turns them into the tier's lines.
replacement: The town's own treasuries' revenue and spending and its firms' sales and cash, read from their books each month and taken out of the state's ledger and sectors line by line.
